correctness.rationale: Over F2 the two removals of the center cancel in the open-neighbor sum, so the equilibrium equation is x_ij=1+r_i+c_j. The row and column sum equations are necessary and sufficient: they ensure prescribed parities are exactly the parities of the reconstructed x, and thus ensure no double counting. They force zero parities for even-even, one constant parity vector and one freely odd vector in mixed parity, and two independently odd parity vectors for odd-odd. In the latter, weight is ab+(m-a)(n-b); both coordinate slopes are nonzero since m and n are odd. Every minimum is a corner, and comparing the four corners gives the claimed counts and the two tied choices for odd squares. Each coordinate of a uniform odd vector of length at least two is fair, giving the stated expectations. Direct tests on six labeled boards, including 3×3 and 3×5, reproduce the weight histograms.
residual_risks: The finite replay checks representative boards; the sufficiency and minimizer arguments establish the general result.
Only pure equilibria, the stated deterministic best response, and labeled fully occupied boards were reviewed.
